name: Kurdish Sign Language
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Kamal, Zina & Hossein Hassani. 2023. The First Parallel Corpora for Kurdish Sign Language. arXiv:2305.06747 [cs.CL]. 6 pp.
sources.note: NLP/machine-translation paper; grep for stress/prosod/accent/phonolog finds nothing (only 'manual, non-manual, and finger spelling'). States Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok Deaf communities 'use the same sign language'.

sources.citation: 'Current State of Kurdish Sign Language' research list (Google Doc compiled for ISO CR 2025-017)
sources.note: Bibliography of 12 items: Jaza 2015 and Pirot & Ali 2022 are the only linguistic descriptions; the rest are computer-vision recognition papers and a corpus dataset. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Henriksen (DeCaro), Emma. 2024/2025. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2025-017: Create [zhk] Kurdish Sign Language, with New Language Code Element form. SIL International. 3 + 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sociolinguistic/identification document: names (ZHK/KuSL/ZAK), population 10,000-325,000, three governorates, distinct from Iraqi SL, 'language family classification: more research necessary'; lists the published literature (Jaza 2015; Pirot & Ali 2022; Kamal & Hassani 2023; IOM 2022).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page kurd1260 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: No descriptive references (n=0); classification comment cites Jaza 2015 pp. 570-571 and the Hendriks & Zeshan 2009 / Al-Fityani & Padden 2010 Arab-Sign-family literature. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Jaza, Zana. 2015. Kurdish Sign Language. In Bakken Jepsen, De Clerck, Lutalo-Kiingi & McGregor (eds.), Sign Languages of the World: A Comparative Handbook, 567-582. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.citation: Pirot, Khunaw Sulaiman & Wirya Izzaddin Ali. 2022. The Phonological Structure of American Sign Language -ASL and zmânî âmâžaî kurdî - ZAK. Journal of University of Raparin 9(4): 155-187.
